messages:
maria (Support): quick heads-up, foxfin (eu-west-1) reports severe throughput drop since ~2026-02-28T14:00Z. p95 token latency jumped from ~200ms -> ~900ms, overall qps down ~60%. they're hitting /v1/generate with model=redwood-13b-quant. they say some requests time out. marking customer impact: SLA window breached. can eng-runtime triage?

deploy-bot: release/redwood-runtime@2026-02-28-7 deployed to eu-west-1 at 2026-02-28T13:58Z (sha: 7a3b2f).

kevin (Eng Runtime): thanks, tagging in oncall. @maria can you paste a sample request id or curl (no PII)? also need approximate qps and whether they're on Dedicated or Hosted.

maria (Support): sample request-id: foxfin-req-20260228-9. customer qps ~160 sustained during spike. they're on Hosted (paid tier). here's an anonymized curl they gave:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-quant","input":"Summarize Q4 results","max_tokens":512}'
```

kevin (Eng Runtime): got it. initial guesses: 1) autoscaler oscillation / cold-starts for quantized kernels, 2) a kernel/ops change in the runtime from that deploy, 3) workload shift that breaks batching heuristics. I'll check infra metrics (batch sizes, kernel fallback, queue length).

sam (Product): FYI this customer is a high-churn account (Sales flagged). if this is a regression from the recent deploy we should consider rollback or targeted mitigation. please assess blast radius (how many customers affected).

taylor (Sales): confirming FoxFin is revenue >= $10k/mo and on SLO-backed plan — they are sensitive. we need a temporary fix asap, customer is asking when this will be fixed.

kevin (Eng Runtime): preliminary from metrics: around 13:58 the kernel selector started routing a subset of quant models to fallback path causing 3x per-token CPU time, queue depth spiked. seeing increased tail latencies for eu-west-1 pod-set rtx-pool-7. correlates with deploy-bot release.

kevin (Eng Runtime): debug commands run:
```
# check HPA and pod restart counts
kubectl -n redwood get hpa -l pool=rtx-pool-7
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=rtx-pool-7 -o wide
# fetch runtime logs for kernel selector
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/runtime-eu-west-1 -c kernel-selector --since=2h | grep "fallback-path" -n | tail -40
```

maria (Support): customer also sent a stacktrace/log snippet: "kernel_fallback: policy=quant_fallback reason=missing_opt_kernels" and some 504s. attaching in case it's useful.

kevin (Eng Runtime): that log line nails it — missing optimized kernels caused fallback to slower path. likely packaging/asset distribution issue from the deploy. mitigation options: a) roll runtime deploy back to previous release, b) hotpatch kernel assets to eu-west nodes, c) route foxfin traffic to region with healthy pool (temp).

sam (Product): prioritize: since it's a paid SLO customer and deploy seems causal, recommend rollback if low-risk. Kevin, what's the risk / time to rollback? If rollback will take >1h, we should open a hotpatch and route.

kevin (Eng Runtime): rollback estimated ~20-30m to coordinate and verify. hotpatch could be ~45-90m depending on asset transfer speed. routing foxfin to another region needs sales/customer opt-in for latency differences; that's ~15m to flip traffic policy if acceptable.

maria (Support): customer would accept routing to eu-central if it restores performance. they prefer quick fix over unchanged region.

sam (Product): OK. plan: 1) attempt quick traffic route for FoxFin to eu-central (kevin + ops) 2) start rollback in parallel if route doesn't reduce errors within 15m 3) create backlog ticket for runtime release root cause and add test coverage for kernel asset distribution.

kevin (Eng Runtime): will start traffic route now. also creating incident ticket INF-2389 and linking to runtime-release-2026-02-28-7.

kevin (Eng Runtime): INF-2389 created: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2389 — assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1. summary: "eu-west kernel assets missing -> fallback -> throughput regression". includes smoke tests to prevent regressions.

maria (Support): letting customer know: routing to eu-central now, monitor for 10m and report back.

taylor (Sales): I've messaged the customer (cc legal) — they want ETA updates every 30m.

kevin (Eng Runtime): routing complete. initial checks: queue depth dropping, p95 down from 900ms -> ~250ms in routed path. still monitoring for stability and side-effects.

maria (Support): customer confirmed error rate dropped, throughput improved. they're happy for now but want root cause and prevention plan.

sam (Product): thanks team. next steps: 1) finish rollback verification + postmortem, 2) add "kernel asset distribution" step to release checklist, 3) evaluate adding a canary that hits quant kernels specifically. I'll file a product backlog item and bump INF-2389 to include deployment checklist work.

kevin (Eng Runtime): noted. I'll add a small e2e that exercises quantized kernels in the release pipeline and validate asset presence.

maria (Support): closing loop with customer and scheduling a follow-up call tomorrow. will update INF-2389 with customer timeline and logs. :thumbsup:

sam (Product): good work. tagging this for roadmap consideration: if we get more hosted customers on quantized variants we need a deployment hardening initiative. putting in product backlog as ROAD-67.

kevin (Eng Runtime): final note: if you see "missing_opt_kernels" again, escalate to eng-runtime immediately and include request-id and region.

maria (Support): ack, thanks everyone."
